# Best portable power station for a CPAP

**My pick: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (1,024 Wh), about $700.** It's the best all-rounder in the guides I found, which are research-based and not hands-on tested.
- It's rated around 20 dB under 200 W, so it's quiet on a nightstand.
- It has a 10 ms UPS switchover, so it takes over if the grid drops while you sleep.
- It recharges from empty in about 49 minutes and weighs 24.9 lb.
- It gets about 2.7 nights with the humidifier off and about 1.7 with it on ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)).
- Prices and "Check on Amazon" and official-store buttons are on [BuyerSheet's CPAP page](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/).

## Other good options

- **Best value: Bluetti AC180 (1,152 Wh).** It's about 3.1 nights humidifier off and 1.4 on. Prices I saw ranged from $449 to $499, and it has a 20 ms UPS. BLUETTI's store lists it at $499, and code AFF5OFF takes $24.95 off, so it's $474.05 ([buy at BLUETTI via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180), an affiliate link). Sources disagree on its weight: one says 16.5 lb, but the spec sheet says about 16 kg (~35 lb), so I'd trust the heavier figure.
- **Best if you want room to grow: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus (1,024 Wh), about $719.** It expands to 5 kWh, which Tested Watts puts at roughly 8 humidifier-on nights, and it's under 30 dB. It weighs 27.6 lb ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)).
- **Cheapest for two nights: EcoFlow RIVER 2 Pro, about $389.** It gets about 2 nights humidifier off but only about 0.9 with it on ([BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/)).
- **Small and light: EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus (286 Wh, 10.4 lb), about $299.** It only covers most of one night with the humidifier off, and about half a night with it on. One guide calls it "multi-night," but the math in the others doesn't support that, so skip it if you use a heated humidifier ([BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/)).

## Things to know

- **Humidifier:** A heated humidifier roughly doubles power use. Turning it off during an outage stretches a charge the most.
- **Sizing:** Plan for at least two nights. Capacity needed is about nightly Wh × nights ÷ 0.85, so 520 Wh × 2 nights comes to roughly 1,200 Wh with the humidifier on.
- **DC cord:** If your CPAP maker sells a 12V DC cord, using it skips inverter losses and adds roughly 10–20% runtime.
- **Jackery caveat:** Jackery says on its product pages that its power stations aren't recommended for medical devices, so I'd skip the Explorer 1000 v2 for CPAP unless your CPAP maker says otherwise.
- **Pure sine wave:** This is required, and all the units above have it.
- **Check your own machine:** Look at your power supply's wattage label, and ask your provider about backup power if you depend on therapy.

If you tell me your CPAP model, whether you use the humidifier, and your budget, I can narrow this to one pick.
